entry_state: The title states a provisional implementation proposal; the contents map the argument from product decision and company cases through representation, methods, language, corporate/group accounting, banking and insurance. The contents continue after insurance acquisition costs; the body has not begun.
exit_state: Chapter 1 establishes that identical historical journals can hide different rate exposures; the first demonstration must preserve alternative company histories, information revisions and conditional statements with traceable assumptions. Forecast accuracy and full sector execution require later evidence. The next chapter must make this concrete for a complete company and a public disclosure.
findings: The remaining contents carry the argument through insurance transition, implementation contracts, validation and distinct portable/historical grammar/research appendices. The last contents page is sparse but its three Appendix C entries are legible.

The opening borrowing example stages principal, annual interest, payment timing and exclusions before its equation. The fixed/floating counterexample establishes why a full journal can still omit economic exposure.
The feasible interval is expressly distinguished from a probability distribution. Generated interpretation counts and model confidence do not supply weights.

The R1–R10 table continues with a repeated header across pages 11–12. The following prose keeps replaceable implementation choices and later bank/insurance execution distinct from representation requirements.

The first demonstration has a positive traceability criterion, three dates, revisions and distinct synthetic/public-case roles. Its success is not presented as forecast accuracy. No confirmed new defect in this segment.

Derivation and first mechanism-bearing example.
I is next-year interest in currency units; principal is 100, alpha is a dimensionless fixed share in [0,1], and rates are annual.
All principal remains outstanding; fixed rate is 0.05, floating rate resets immediately to 0.07 for the whole year; fees, default, hedges and FX are excluded.
This is a local exact algebraic calculation: 100 times the weighted rates expands to 5 alpha plus 7 minus 7 alpha, hence 7 minus 2 alpha.
Alpha zero gives 7; alpha one gives 5. The negative slope reflects replacing higher-rate floating borrowing with fixed borrowing.
